subject: Recap: Private deployment discovery for FinSecure — next steps & checklist
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finsecure.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Johnson <m.johnson@finsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment discovery — quick follow-up and summary

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the call today — quick recap from my side and a couple of clarifying items before we schedule the tech deep-dive with your infra team.

Key pain points we described:
- Regulatory scope: PCI + SOC2 + state-level financial regs; any vendor must provide auditable logs and retention controls.
- Network constraints: most services are in an isolated on-prem VPC with strict egress (only explicit IP allowlist); no general internet egress allowed.
- KMS: must use customer-managed keys (HSM or our existing cloud KMS appliance) and a key-rotation policy controlled by our security team.
- Air-gap considerations: some environments are air-gapped and require offline installation media and manual updates.
- Performance: current in-house LLM inference has high variance; goal is stable 99th percentile latency and predictable cost per token.

Current stack (short):
- On-prem Kubernetes (Rancher-managed) running internal services; private Oracle DB; internal SSO (SAML).
- We currently self-host an open-source model stack on a handful of GPUs but have reliability and ops maturity gaps.

Success criteria for initial PoC:
- Deployment inside our VPC with no outbound internet besides whitelisted endpoints.
- Support for customer-managed KMS and clear audit logs pushed to our SIEM.
- Documented installation procedure for air-gapped install OR an appliance-based option.
- Demo that shows stable p95/p99 latency and throughput for our workload (~5–10 concurrent streams, bursts to 50 qps).

Next steps I proposed:
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/solutions engineering (include steps for network, KMS, and air-gap).
- Exchange of network diagram and list of required IPs/ports.
- Redwood to share a short checklist and SOC2 evidence request so our security team can start a review.

I've attached our vendor-assessments.pdf (high level) and will share the internal network diagram before the deep-dive.

Best,
Elena
Director, Infrastructure Security
FinSecure

---
Attachment: finsecure-vendor-assessments.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mark Johnson <m.johnson@finsecure.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 17:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment discovery — quick follow-up and summary

Thanks Elena — great summary and very helpful. Confirming our understanding and listing concrete next steps so we all have the same checklist before the deep-dive.

Confirmed understanding:
- Must support deployment inside FinSecure-managed VPCs with strict egress allowlist.
- Customer-managed KMS required (we support HSM-backed KMS integrations and can run with external KMS via mTLS).
- Air-gapped installs: we can provide an offline installer and documented manual upgrade path; will surface any OS/package licensing caveats up front.
- Audit/logging: Redwood can export structured audit logs and per-request traces to your SIEM (we'll need the schema mapping).

Proposed next steps and owners:
1) Technical deep-dive (60–90 min): include your infra/security + our infra engineer (Vivek) and solutions architect (Priyom). Owner: Neha to coordinate scheduling.
2) Share network diagram + allowlist requirements: Elena to send a diagram and list of IP ranges/ports. Owner: FinSecure.
3) SOC2/evidence packet: Neha to send a soc2-evidence-request.xlsx (template) and our attestation and encryption whitepaper. Owner: Neha.
4) PoC scope doc: Redwood to draft PoC scope (configuration, success metrics, duration) after deep-dive. Owner: Priyom.

Questions we have before the deep-dive (short):
- Expected steady-state and burst TPS (you mentioned bursts to ~50 qps, can you confirm requests per minute and average payload size)?
- Any data residency constraints beyond on-prem (e.g., which environments must be air-gapped)?

I've attached the soc2-evidence-request.xlsx template and a short architecture note outlining our on-prem packaging options. Vivek, please flag anything missing from the engineering checklist below.

Looking forward to the deep-dive — I've proposed two 60–90 minute slots in the calendar invite that I will send after you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: soc2-evidence-request.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)
Attachment: redwood-onprem-arch-diagram.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB)
From: Mark Johnson <m.johnson@finsecure.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment discovery — quick follow-up and summary

Thanks both — quick answers to Neha's clarifying questions from our side.

Traffic profile:
- Expected steady-state: ~600 requests per hour (avg payload ~2KB).
- Peak bursts: short spikes up to ~3,000 requests in 10-minute windows (we expect Redwood to handle burst smoothing or fallback).

Retention/PII:
- We need logs for 12 months for audit but only redacted request content (we can accept token-level metadata instead of raw prompts).

Environments:
- Two environments need to be fully air-gapped (fraud analysis and payments). One environment (research) can have controlled egress.

I'll send the network diagram tonight and confirm which environments map to which clusters. If you can include a short note in the PoC scope about how rollbacks are handled in air-gapped installs that would be great.

Mark
VP Product Operations
FinSecure

---
Attachment: (will attach network diagram in follow-up)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mark Johnson <m.johnson@finsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment discovery — quick follow-up and summary

On Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 08:12 AM Mark Johnson <m.johnson@finsecure.com> wrote:
> Traffic profile:
> - Expected steady-state: ~600 requests per hour (avg payload ~2KB).
> - Peak bursts: short spikes up to ~3,000 requests in 10-minute windows...

Thanks — I'll join the deep-dive. A couple of notes from engineering perspective and items we'll want to confirm during the call:

Prelim engineering assumptions:
- We can support private deployment via an operator that installs into your Kubernetes clusters (Helm + operator). For fully air-gapped clusters we'll provide an image bundle + installer instructions.
- Customer-managed KMS: we support gRPC mTLS to external HSMs and can integrate with on-prem KMS appliances; need to validate cipher suites.
- Audit logs: we will stream structured logs to a local collector endpoint (Fluentd/Logstash) or write to an internal S3-compatible store.

Engineering checklist for deep-dive (please have these items available):
1) Network diagram + CIDR ranges and whether NAT is allowed for specific clusters.
2) Egress allowlist policy and any proxy/jump-host requirements.
3) KMS appliance details (model/version), certs for mTLS if available.
4) Cluster admin contact and preferred method for offline install media transfer (SCP, USB, secure courier).
5) Expected retention windows for logs and if redaction requirements are automated or manual.

We'll also prepare a short demo showing p95/p99 under a synthetic workload similar to your profile. Priyom will draft PoC scope immediately after the deep-dive and capture rollback/upgrade steps for air-gapped clusters.

See you on the call — I'll add two proposed deep-dive slots to the invite thread.

Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
